Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: relevantOccupation

candidates.label: hasMolecularFunction

Examples: "A protein has a molecular function of enzyme activity.", "This BioChemEntity has a molecular function described by a defined term.", "The entity's molecular function is specified."

candidates.label: educationalRole
candidates.comment: An educational role relation between an educational audience and the text describing its specific role. Also called "audience role", "learner role", "student type". candidates.label: numberedPosition

candidates.label: qualifications

candidates.label: position

candidates.label: chemicalRole

candidates.label: subjectOf

Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". candidates.label: associatedClaimReview

candidates.label: observationAbout

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage

Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: studySubject

Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: mainContentOfPage

Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: event

Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: activityDuration
candidates.comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property indicates the subject matter or topic of an event, which aligns with its purpose.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: businessFunction
candidates.comment: A characterization of the business function associated with a demand, offer, or component of a bundle. Also called "purpose of offer", "transaction type", "commercial role". Examples: "Product offer businessFunction Sell", "Car lease offer businessFunction Lease", "Repair service offer businessFunction Repair".

candidates.label: contactType
candidates.comment: A classification relation for a contact point, specifying its purpose or kind. Also called "type of contact", "contact purpose", "department". Examples: "Phone number contact point contactType 'Sales'", "Email address contact point contactType 'Support'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: audience
candidates.comment: An intended group for whom a creative work, event, lodging business, play action, product, or service was created. Also called: target group, demographic, intended recipient. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Children's Book' audience 'Children'", "Event 'Tech Conference' audience 'Developers'", "Product 'Luxury Car' audience 'High-net-worth individuals'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: quest
candidates.comment: A quest relation between a game or video game series and a specific task or mission that players can complete for a reward. Also called mission, task, objective. Examples: "A role-playing game features a quest to 'defeat the dragon'.", "A video game series includes a quest to 'collect all artifacts'.", "An adventure game has a quest to 'rescue the princess'."

candidates.label: responsibilities
candidates.comment: A description of the duties and tasks associated with a job posting or occupation. Also called duties, tasks, job functions, accountabilities. Examples: `Software Engineer Job Posting` responsibilities `"Develop and maintain web applications"`, `Marketing Manager Occupation` responsibilities `"Oversee campaign strategy"`, `Doctor Job` responsibilities `"Diagnose and treat patients"`.

chosen_property.label: preferredCandidate
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a person who is the preferred candidate of an organization.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly links an Organization to its preferred candidate.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: acceptedAnswer
candidates.comment: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."

candidates.label: pronouns
candidates.comment: A pronoun relation between a person and the linguistic terms they use to refer to themselves. Also called preferred pronouns, self-identification pronouns. Examples: "A person uses pronouns 'she/her'.", "Another person uses pronouns 'they/them'.", "A third person uses pronouns 'he/him'."

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: applicantLocationRequirements
candidates.comment: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: suggestedMeasurement
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing a suggested range of body measurements for an intended audience or person, often for wearable products. Also called "size recommendation", "body measurement range", "fit guide", "sizing suggestion". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedMeasurement inseam 32-34 inches", "The size specification includes suggestedMeasurement height 170-190 cm", "This product is designed for a suggestedMeasurement chest 40-42 inches."

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".
